name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.selected_commonFixedProjection_eq_zero
title: An inequivalent GNS fiber has no residual common range

content.assumptions:
Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra, the completion of the matrix stages $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$. Write $f_n$ for the image of the first diagonal matrix unit. These are decreasing projections with $f_0=1$. Write $\iota_n$ for the canonical embedding of stage $n$. The root state $\omega$ is determined by $\omega(\iota_n(a))=a_{00}$ on every stage.

Choose one pure state $\varphi_j$ from each unitary-equivalence class $j\in I$ of pure-state Gelfand-Naimark-Segal (GNS) representations, retaining $\omega$ at the root index $o$. Write $(H_j,\pi_j,\xi_j)$ for its complete complex GNS space, unital star representation and unit cyclic vector. Thus $\varphi_j(a)=\langle\xi_j,\pi_j(a)\xi_j\rangle$, and the vectors $\pi_j(a)\xi_j$ are dense in $H_j$. Inner products are linear in the second argument.

A fixed shell family supplies unital complex star automorphisms $\alpha_j$ and elements $w_{j,n}\in A$ with $\varphi_j\circ\alpha_j=\omega$, $w_{j,n}^*w_{j,n}=\alpha_j(f_n-f_{n+1})$, and $w_{j,n}w_{j,n}^*=f_n-f_{n+1}$. At the root, $\alpha_o$ is the identity and $w_{o,n}=f_n-f_{n+1}$. Fix $i\in I$ and put $f_{i,n}=\alpha_i(f_n)$. The family is supplied; its existence is not an extra conclusion here. The condition $j\ne i$ means that the unitary-equivalence classes are distinct, not merely that two state functionals in the same class differ. The selected representation $\pi_j$ is irreducible and has nonzero Hilbert space because $\|\xi_j\|=1$.
content.conclusion: The transported flag leaves no nonzero vector fixed in an inequivalent chosen fiber. As a separate consequence of decreasing orthogonal projections, $\pi_j(f_{i,n})x\to0$ in norm for each fixed $x\in H_j$. Thus the surviving line in the matching fiber is sharply separated from every other chosen class.
content.display_title: An inequivalent GNS fiber has no residual common range
content.lean_realization_notes: Irreducibility is used to make a nonzero candidate fixed vector cyclic. The conclusion is not asserted for an arbitrary reducible representation or for a different vector state in the same GNS class. The exact source proves equality of projections; strong convergence uses the additional cited projection theorem and does not imply operator-norm convergence.
content.natural_language_statement: Fix a shell family and indices $i,j\in I$ as below, with $j\ne i$. For $f_{i,n}=\alpha_i(f_n)$, let $F_j=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\operatorname{ran}\pi_j(f_{i,n})$ and let $P_j$ be its orthogonal projection. Then $P_j=0$, or equivalently $F_j=\{0\}$.
content.one_sentence_role: Uses compression and cyclic transport to exclude fixed vectors in every other chosen pure-state class.

proof_steps.text: If $P_j\ne0$, choose $z$ with $P_jz\ne0$ and normalize $P_jz$ to a unit vector $\eta$. Since $P_j$ projects onto the common range, every $\pi_j(f_{i,n})$ fixes $\eta$.

Take the matrix coefficient of the represented compression error against $\eta$. Fixedness and unit norm turn it into the constant $\langle\eta,\pi_j(b)\eta\rangle-\varphi_i(b)$; norm convergence forces this constant to vanish.

The orbit closures of $\xi_i$ and $\eta$ are their full Hilbert spaces. Equality of vector states gives equality of orbit inner products, so the map $\pi_i(b)\xi_i\mapsto\pi_j(b)\eta$ extends to a surjective complex-linear isometry that intertwines the representations. This contradicts $j\ne i$.

content.proof_summary: If $F_j$ contained a unit vector $\eta$, [the transported CAR compression estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/AtomicSource.lean#L150-L161) $\|f_{i,n} b f_{i,n}-\varphi_i(b)f_{i,n}\|\to0$, valid for every $b\in A$, would imply $\langle\eta,\pi_j(b)\eta\rangle=\varphi_i(b)$. Irreducibility makes $\eta$ cyclic. Equality of this vector state with the state of $\xi_i$ yields a unitary intertwiner from $\pi_i$ to $\pi_j$, contradicting their distinct classes.
